text: Skinny cattle with rough, discolored hair and an exhausted look are a common sight in Cambodia, and recovery isn't quick. Main causes: insufficient feeding (quality and quantity) is by far the leading cause — multivitamin injections or stimulants alone aren't enough; the fix is distributing good-quality grass (for protein) and/or a Home Made Concentrate; recovering proper condition on an adequate energy/protein diet takes about 6 weeks. Late weaning: it's not unusual to see calves over 6 months still suckling — if the cow doesn't get feed supplements to sustain milk production alongside this, she draws on her own reserves and loses condition; weaning calves before 6 months prevents this (and note that a skinny cow won't show estrus). Parasitism: heavy worm burdens hurt body condition, and Liver Fluke specifically can cause severe wasting once anemia sets in — deworm cattle twice a year (start and end of the rainy season), especially for group-grazing cattle on wet pasture. Blood parasites: Babesia, Trypanosoma, and likely Anaplasma circulate in Cambodia; Trypanosoma is regularly found in cattle though its exact impact on body condition isn't always clear — if poor condition comes with intermittent high fever and eye discharge, injecting Berenil to address Trypanosoma is recommended.
